questions.question: Day 6 Scenario (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs): Select the natural English phrasing when My sister is inviting neighbors for tea by 5:00 PM:

options.a: Please drop by our place this evening for tea.
options.b: Evening come my house tea.
options.c: Evening come my house tea. yesterday
options.d: I am inviting neighbors for tea right now.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural everyday English uses standard tense agreement: "Please drop by our place this evening for tea.".

questions.question: Day 6 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'circle back'?

options.a: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.b: Return to a topic later for follow-up.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

questions.question: Day 6 Vocabulary (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'follow up'?

options.a: Check progress on a prior matter.
options.b: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.c: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.
options.d: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'follow up' means: check progress on a prior matter. Example: "I will follow up with the team regarding the report."

questions.question: Day 6 Terms (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs): Choose the correct definition for the phrasal verb 'touch base':

questions.question:
Day 6 Translation Scenario 1 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.b: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.c: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: In agreement some changes if do good.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 6 Telugu Scenario 2 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs):

Telugu: "అన్నా, బస్టాండ్ దగ్గర డ్రాప్ చేయండి, ఎంత అవుతుంది?"
(Word-by-word: "Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?
options.c: I am needing to brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?
options.d: Brother bus stand drop me, how much will become?

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "Please drop me off near the bus stand. How much is the fare?"

Avoid 'how much will become' and ask 'How much is the fare?'.

questions.question:
Day 6 Translation Scenario 3 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs):

Telugu: "రేపటి మీటింగ్ 3 గంటలకు రీషెడ్యూల్ చేయవచ్చా?"
(Literal attempt: "Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?")

options.a: Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?
options.b: Tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.c: I am needing to tomorrow meeting 3 clock reschedule possible?
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
Natural Version: "Could we reschedule tomorrow's meeting to 3:00 PM?"

Use 'Could we reschedule...' for polite professional requests.

questions.question:
Day 6 Translation Scenario 4 (Technical Demos & Walkthroughs):

Telugu: "నేను సాధారణంగా ఉదయం 6 గంటలకే నిద్రలేచి ఒక కప్పు టీ తాగుతాను."
(Literal attempt: "I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.")

options.a: I am needing to i generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.
options.b: I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: I generally in morning 6 clock wake up drink tea.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "I usually wake up at 6:00 AM and have a cup of tea."

Use 'have a cup of tea' and specify time as '6:00 AM'.
